Interview prompt: "Tell me about a performance problem you solved."
fields.Back:
S: BMO's transaction batch-processing pipeline handled 2.5M+ account records per day and latency was a bottleneck.
T: Speed up the core calculation logic without breaking existing Python-based integrations.
A: Rewrote the hot path as a C++20 financial calculation engine and exposed it to the rest of the system via pybind11 bindings.
R: Cut batch-processing latency by 42% at that 2.5M+ record/day scale.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Describe a large-scale modernization effort you contributed to."
fields.Back:
S: BMO had 30+ legacy APIs on older, tightly-coupled infrastructure.
T: Modernize them to a scalable, maintainable architecture.
A: Migrated the APIs to serverless, event-driven services built on AWS Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, CloudWatch, and SQS.
R: 30+ APIs now run on serverless infrastructure, improving scalability and observability.

fields.Front: Interview prompt: "Tell me about a tool you built to improve developer productivity."
fields.Back:
S: Engineers needed to manually dig through CloudWatch logs and pre-deploy code review was slow/inconsistent.
T: Build tooling to speed up both log investigation and code quality checks.
A: Built a Python CLI to search/filter CloudWatch logs, and custom Python linting/static-analysis scripts for C++ and Node.js running on AWS CodeBuild.
R: 40% faster log retrieval; 30% faster builds and 20% fewer pre-deploy defects from the linting tooling.

fields.Text: Michele engineered a high-throughput financial calculation engine in {{c1::C++20}} with {{c2::Python (pybind11)}} bindings, cutting batch-processing latency {{c3::42%}} across {{c4::2.5M+}} daily account records.
The legacy APIs were modernized into serverless, event-driven architectures using {{c1::AWS Lambda}}, {{c2::API Gateway}}, {{c3::DynamoDB}}, {{c4::CloudWatch}}, and {{c5::AWS SQS}}.
